title: Paper LBO
objectives: Answer out loud: $100 EBITDA, 10x entry, 5x leverage, EBITDA grows to $130, $150 paid down, exit at 10x. What are MOIC and IRR? (1.9x, ~14%)

blocks.body: Five steps in your head, with no Excel:

steps.heading: Sources
steps.body: debt (EBITDA × leverage multiple); equity = price − debt.

steps.heading: Project
steps.body: EBITDA growth and cumulative free cash flow over the holding period.

steps.heading: Exit
steps.body: exit EBITDA × exit multiple − remaining debt = exit equity.

steps.heading: Returns
steps.body: MOIC = exit equity ÷ initial equity; estimate IRR with rules of thumb.

blocks.title: How do you estimate IRR without a calculator?
blocks.teaser: Memorize anchors: 2x in 3 years ≈ 26%, 2x in 5 ≈ 15%, 2.5x in 5 ≈ 20%, 3x in 5 ≈ 25%, 3x in 3 ≈ 44%.
blocks.body: Memorize anchors: 2x in 3 years ≈ 26%, 2x in 5 ≈ 15%, 2.5x in 5 ≈ 20%, 3x in 5 ≈ 25%, 3x in 3 ≈ 44%. Interpolate between them. Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ rate.

blocks.prompt: A sponsor triples its money over 5 years. Roughly what IRR is that?
blocks.explanation: Anchor: 3x in 5 years ≈ 25%. (3x in 3 years ≈ 44%; 2x in 5 years ≈ 15%.)

blocks.title: What simplifications are acceptable in a paper LBO?
blocks.teaser: Ignore fees, round taxes, assume all FCF pays down debt, and use simple growth.
blocks.body: Ignore fees, round taxes, assume all FCF pays down debt, and use simple growth. The interviewer is testing your logic and speed, not decimal precision.

blocks.title: How would you solve for the maximum price to hit 25% IRR?
blocks.teaser: Work backwards: 25% IRR over 5 years ≈ 3.0x MOIC.
blocks.body: Work backwards: 25% IRR over 5 years ≈ 3.0x MOIC. Required equity = exit equity ÷ 3.0. Maximum purchase price = required equity + debt raised.

blocks.title: Say it out loud
prompts: $100 EBITDA, 10x entry, 5x leverage, EBITDA grows to $130, $150 paid down, exit at 10x. What are MOIC and IRR? (1.9x, ~14%)
